# Welcome to the course!


-   Welcome to the `inlabru` workshop!
-   Over one day, we'll introduce Bayesian hierarchical modelling with `inlabru`, focusing on spatial models for ecological data.
-   The day alternates short lectures with hands-on practicals.
-   Workshop materials are available in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/inlabru-courses/ISEC2027).



::: {.callout-warning}
##  Important! ⚠️

 Please use the instructions provided [here](Install_software.qmd) to install and check your installation
  *before* the course starts.
:::

# Learning objectives

By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to:

- **specify, fit and interpret** Bayesian hierarchical models in `inlabru`;
- **explain** why hierarchical (latent Gaussian) models are relevant in spatial ecology, and how `inlabru` fits them with INLA;
- **build** spatial models — continuous fields (SPDE) and point processes (LGCP) — and **map** their predictions;

# Intended audience

The workshop aims to cater for participants with a range of different backgrounds, who are interested in analysing data with modern spatial statistical modelling approaches.

# Prerequisites

Participants should be familiar with the `R` environment, and general statistical approaches for modelling such as regression, analysis of (co)variance, and generalized linear models.

No knowledge of `R-INLA` or `inlabru` is required.
